newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria says still seeks peace with Israel.
newsitem.headline: Syria says still seeks peace with Israel.

text.p: Syria is still committed to making peace with Israel but is ready in case the Jewish state resorts to war, a senior official told a rally in the Syrian capital on Saturday.

Abdullah al-Ahmar, assistant secretary-general of the ruling Baath party, said at celebrations marking the 26th anniversary of President Hafez al-Assad's coming to power that Syria insisted on Israel's withdrawal from the Golan Heights as a condition for peace.
Syria was "honest in its search for a just and comprehensive peace...that requires an Israeli withdrawal from the Golan", he said.

"As we work to strengthen our way to a just and comprehensive peace through negotiations, we do not ignore other possibilities and options which Israel might resort to: such as an armed attack against Syria and Lebanon to escape the international pressures," he said.
Israel and Syria have accused each other over the last month of preparing for war.

On-off Syrian-Israeli peace talks received another setback last June when Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu took office and rejected trading Arab lands for peace, the principle underpinning Middle East peace negotiations since 1991.
Assad came to power in Syria in a bloodless coup in November 1970.
